premises: Heterogeneous grain structures in low-SFE alloys generate back-stress hardening that sustains strain hardening over large strains.
Deformation twinning can be activated during high-strain-rate loading in low-SFE alloys, enhancing strain hardening and delaying shear localization.
The proposed warm rolling and partial recrystallization treatment can produce a heterogeneous nano-to-micro grain structure with retained twins in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The back-stress and twin-based hardening mechanisms observed in FCC CrCoNi and Al0.3CoCrFeNi will operate similarly in the BCC HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy.
